newsitem.title: USA: Duke Oconee nuke seen back up this weekend.
newsitem.headline: Duke Oconee nuke seen back up this weekend.

text.p: Duke Power Co's 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee nuclear power unit 2 should resume power output this weekend after shutting in September following an accident which injured several workers, a spokesman said.
"We are currently conducting startup activities, we expect to bring it up over the weekend," spokesman Rick Zuercher said Thursday.
The unit, in Seneca, S.C., was shut Sept 24 after a steam pipe burst in the non-nuclear part of the plant. Seven workers were scalded in the incident, four of them critically.
The adjacent Oconee units 1 and 3, each with a capacity of 846 MW, were shut Oct 4 for steam pipe inspections.
Units 1 and 3 are expected to resume power production in February.
Work on all three units included replacement of some pipes and the addition of check valves and drain valves, the spokesman said.
Oconee 2 is expected to reach full power output about three days after synchronizing to the grid, Zuercher said.
The Oconee plant's overall generation capacity is 2,538 MW.
Duke Power has a total generating capacity of about 18,500 MW of which the Oconoee plant accounts for about 14 percent.
